title: Why one apple half goes brown
pause_note: Channel v5, first Kitchen Science Short. WEIRD hook: same apple, one half browning at 0 s; wrong guess (rot) killed at ~4 s; reveal (cells burst, enzyme spills) at ~7 s; a visible change every <= 2.5 s; payoff = lemon half; loop to two halves; one-word question.

beats: Same apple, same cut. So why is only one half going brown?
It isn't rot. The apple is doing it to itself.
An enzyme spills out onto the fruit's own polyphenols.
Add oxygen, and it turns them into quinones that clump into brown pigment.
The white half got lemon juice.
Acid slows the enzyme, and vitamin C undoes its first step.
Would you still eat the brown half?
